front.title: BMP YANG Model for Network Telemetry Messages

abstract.t: This document defines an extensible message schema in YANG to be used at BMP collectors to transform BMP messages into messages which are consumed by external systems such as Message Brokers.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: Nowadays network operators are using BGP Monitoring Protocol (BMP) to monitor the BGP peerings and RIB's. With a machine and human readable extensible Network Telemetry message schema in YANG has been defined.
Network operators organize their data in a Data Mesh where a Message Broker such as Apache Kafka or Apache Pulsar facilitates the exchange of messages among data processing components.
YANG Message Keys for Message Broker Integration describes how Dimensional YANG data can be indexed and addressed in Message Brokers.

This document describes how defined Network Telemetry message is being extended to support BMP data transformation to YANG at the BMP Network Telemetry data collector and being indexed and addressed in Message Broker based on principles at the YANG Message Broker Producer.

section.name: Conventions and Definitions
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.

section.name: Terminology
section.t: The following terms are used as defined in :
The following terms are used as defined in :
The following terms are used as defined in Apache Kafka and Apache Pulsar Message Broker:

ul.li: Subject: Is used for Messages within a Topic sharing the same schema tree and also to identify a unique schema tree within a schema registry.
Topic: A communication channel for publishing and subscribing messages with one or more subjects and partitions.
Topic Compaction: The act of compressing messages in a topic to the latest state. As used with Apache Pulsar. Apache Kafka uses the term Log Compaction with identical meaning.
Partition: Messages in a topic are spread over hash buckets where a hash bucket refers to a partition being stored on one message broker node. Message ordering is guaranteed within a partition.
Message: A piece of structured data sent between data processing components to facilitate communication in a distributed system
Message Key: Metadata associated with a message to facilitate deterministic hash bucketing and indexing for instantiated YANG data.
Message Value: The content of a message, carried alongside its Message Key and headers.
Partition Key: Metadata associated with a message to facilitate deterministic hash bucketing for instantiated YANG data. Also known as ordering key or routing key.

ul.li: BMP Index: A unique identifier created depending on BMP Message Type from multiple BMP and BGP data dimensions. The BMP Index is used to generate the Message Key. See .

section.name: Relationship to draft-ietf-nmop-message-broker-telemetry-message
section.t: defines, using the 'ietf-telemetry-message' YANG module, a base Network Telemetry Message schema used between Message Broker Producer and Message Broker Consumer, and using the 'ietf-yang-push-telemetry-message' YANG module, an extension that supports YANG-Push specific subscription metadata.

This document defines five BMP YANG modules , , , , and two BGP YANG modules , . The 'ietf-bmp-message' module, together with the modules it imports, defines the BMP messages, which can be used on their own or populate the anydata "payload" node defined in the 'ietf-telemetry-message' YANG module of . The 'ietf-bmp-telemetry-message' module extends 'ietf-telemetry-message' for BMP in the same way as 'ietf-yang-push-telemetry-message' does for YANG-Push: it defines the BMP session protocol and adds BMP session metadata to the Network Telemetry protocol metadata.

section.name: Relationship to draft-ietf-idr-bgp-model
section.t: defines the 'ietf-bgp' YANG module along with the following submodules: 'ietf-bgp-capabilities', 'ietf-bgp-common', 'ietf-bgp-common-errors', 'ietf-bgp-common-multiprotocol', 'ietf-bgp-neighbor', 'ietf-bgp-rib', 'ietf-bgp-rib-attributes', and 'ietf-bgp-rib-tables'. It further defines the standalone modules 'ietf-bgp-types', 'ietf-bgp-community-types', 'ietf-bgp-policy', and 'ietf-bgp-session-security', and the IANA-maintained modules 'iana-bgp-afi-safi-types', 'iana-bgp-capabilities', 'iana-bgp-community-types', 'iana-bgp-notification', and 'iana-bgp-rib-types'.

This document defines two new standalone YANG modules, 'ietf-bgp-rib-entry' and 'ietf-bgp-open', that import 'ietf-bgp'. 'ietf-bgp-rib-entry' also imports 'iana-bgp-afi-safi-types' for the AFI-SAFI identities and 'ietf-bgp-types' for BGP attribute types. The 'ietf-bgp-rib-entry' module adapts the groupings exposed by the 'ietf-bgp-rib', 'ietf-bgp-rib-attributes', and 'ietf-bgp-rib-tables' submodules and restructures them into a 'rib-entry' grouping that represents a single BGP RIB entry suitable for serialization in a Telemetry Message on a Message Broker. The 'clear-routes' YANG grouping has been omitted since a Telemetry Message covers only operational metrics. The 'ietf-bgp-open' module exposes BGP OPEN message fields for use in BMP Peer Up notifications.

Because 'ietf-bgp-rib-attributes' and 'ietf-bgp-rib-tables' are YANG submodules that belong to the 'ietf-bgp' main module, they cannot be imported independently. This document therefore, imports the full 'ietf-bgp' module, which includes BGP configuration and policy content that is not required for telemetry purposes.

Once 'ietf-bgp-rib-attributes' and 'ietf-bgp-rib-tables' are restructured as standalone importable modules, this document could be simplified to import only those specific modules rather than the entire 'ietf-bgp' and its submodules. Such a change requires coordination with the authors on an appropriate timeline. This section will be removed if and once those changes are in place.
The authors are honored under for their contribution to the BGP YANG modelling this document uses.

section.name: Relationship to draft-ietf-grow-bmp-yang
section.t: defines the 'ietf-bmp' YANG module for the configuration and monitoring of BMP. While there is no direct relationship between this document and its defined YANG modules, it is worth mentioning that BMP data subscribed to with is transformed at BMP monitoring stations to Message Brokers as described in this document.

section.name: Carrying BMP Messages in Network Telemetry Messages
section.t: A BMP message modeled by 'ietf-bmp-message' can be published to the Message Broker on its own, forming the Message Value, or carried in the "payload" of a Network Telemetry Message defined by the 'ietf-telemetry-message' module of , which then forms the Message Value. The Network Telemetry Message adds metadata about the network node, the data collector, and the BMP session, such as the session-start-timestamp and the cached Initiation information, that a BMP message on its own does not carry.
When a Network Telemetry Message is used, its nodes other than "payload" carry two kinds of metadata:

ul.li: Nodes defined by 'ietf-telemetry-message' for any Network Telemetry protocol. defines how they are populated for BMP.
BMP specific nodes defined by this document in 'ietf-bmp-telemetry-message', described in .

section.name: Network Telemetry Message Nodes
section.t: This section describes how each child of the top-level message node of 'ietf-telemetry-message' is populated from the BMP message and the BMP session it was received on.

section.name: network-node-manifest
section.t: The network-node-manifest describes the monitored router. lists the rules for its nodes.

tr.td: name

Hostname of the router, the same value as the node hostname in the Message Key and the Partition Key. If the collector has no other source for it, the sysName of the Initiation message SHOULD be used.
other nodes
Optional, from the collector's knowledge of the router.

section.name: data-collection-manifest
section.t: The data-collection-manifest describes the BMP data collector that received the BMP message and produced the Network Telemetry Message, for example its name ("bmp-collector-1"), vendor, and software-version. This allows a consumer to identify the collector that decoded the BMP data, e.g., when several collectors publish to the same topic.

section.name: network-operator-metadata
section.t: The network-operator-metadata carries optional labels added by the network operator. This document defines no BMP specific labels.

section.name: telemetry-message-metadata
section.t: The telemetry-message-metadata carries the Network Telemetry protocol metadata of the BMP session. lists the rules for its nodes; the bmp-session container added by this document is described in .

tr.td: node-export-timestamp

The Timestamp TLV of type message-export-time if present; otherwise absent. The Per-Peer Header Timestamp is not used, as it is defined as the time at which the routes were received or installed in the RIB (, ), not the time at which the BMP message was exported.
collection-timestamp
Time at which the collector received the BMP message.
notification-event

"log" for messages derived from a BMP message received from the monitored router. "delete" when the collector removes cached state that the router did not explicitly withdraw, for example the routes of a peer after a Peer Down, or all state of the router when the BMP session ends, with or without a Termination message.
sequence-number
As defined in 'ietf-telemetry-message': incremented by the collector for every published message.
session-protocol
The bmp identity defined in 'ietf-bmp-telemetry-message'. It enables the bmp-session container.
export-address, export-port
IP address and TCP port of the monitored router for the BMP session. The port usually changes with every new BMP session and is not used to identify the router.
collection-address, collection-port
IP address and TCP port of the collector for the BMP session.

section.t: The sequence-number of the Network Telemetry Message lets a consumer detect gaps in the messages published by a collector. To detect loss or reordering within a BMP session, a consumer uses the BMP Sequence Number TLV when the monitored router sends it.

section.name: BMP Session Metadata
section.t: The 'ietf-bmp-telemetry-message' module augments telemetry-message-metadata with the bmp-session container. It is present only when session-protocol is bmp and carries metadata that is not part of any BMP message: the data collector derives it from the BMP session and from earlier messages of that session. lists its nodes.

tr.td: session-start-timestamp

Mandatory. Time at which the data collector established the BMP session with the monitored router. All messages of the same BMP session carry the same value; a new value indicates a new BMP session, for example after a reconnect.
initiation-information
Content of the Initiation message of the BMP session (sysName, sysDescr, and strings), cached by the data collector.
bgp-session/peer-up-timestamp

Time of the Peer Up message that started the monitored BGP session the message relates to, taken from that Peer Up message: the Timestamp TLV of type trigger-time if present; otherwise the Per-Peer Header Timestamp if non-zero; otherwise its collection-timestamp. For a Peer Up sent when the BMP session comes up, this can be the time of the BMP session rather than of the BGP session. Absent for messages without a peer (Initiation, Termination).
bgp-session/rib-sync-state

Route Monitoring messages only. Whether the message is part of the initial synchronization of the RIB (initial-sync), is the End-of-RIB marker that completes it (end-of-rib), or is an update of an already synchronized RIB (synchronized). The RIB is identified by the peer, the AFI/SAFI, and the RIB type of the message. Absent if the collector cannot determine it.

section.t: Because uses Route Monitoring messages both for the initial synchronization and for the ongoing monitoring of the Adj-RIB-In, a consumer can use the session-start-timestamp and the rib-sync-state to interpret a Peer Up and the following Route Monitoring messages as the synchronization of a new session rather than as route changes. The bmp-session nodes are not part of the Message Key.

A BMP Initiation message is sent once per BMP session, and the following messages carry no router identity information. A data collector that carries BMP messages in Network Telemetry Messages SHOULD therefore cache the Initiation message content for each BMP session and populate initiation-information in every message it emits, so that each message is self-contained for consumers that did not observe or store the Initiation message.

section.name: YANG Message Broker BMP Indexing and Topic Naming
section.t: To identify which network node produced which BMP data into which Message Broker Topic, Partition and Subject, BMP Message Keys, Partition Key, and Indexes are being introduced (). These keys enable a deterministic distribution of BMP messages across Topics and Partitions enabling applications to consume only the needed data from specific topics and partitions.

section.name: BMP Message Keys and Indexes
section.t: A Message Broker uses a Message Key for indexing and enabling Topic Compaction. While a Message Key can also drive deterministic partition assignment, this document introduces a dedicated Partition Key for that purpose, as described in .

Similar to for YANG-Push telemetry messages, the network node hostname and a set of 'ietf-bmp-message' YANG nodes from the instance data are used to construct the BMP Message Key. The following subsections describe and illustrate the YANG nodes used for each BMP message type.

For all BMP message types that carry a BMP Per-Peer Header (Peer Up, Peer Down, Statistics Report, Route Monitoring, and Route Mirroring), the Message Key consists of the node hostname and a YANG instance-identifier path encoding the message-type and the following per-peer header nodes to uniquely identify the BGP peering session:

dl.dd: Scopes the session to its routing instance: Global Instance Peer, RD Instance Peer, Local Instance Peer, or Loc-RIB Instance Peer.

The Route Distinguisher of the routing instance. Zero-filled for Global Instance Peers; non-zero for RD Instance and possibly Loc-RIB Instance Peers to distinguish sessions within the same VRF or routing instance.
The remote IP address associated with the BGP session.
The AS number of the remote BGP speaker.
The BGP Identifier of the remote BGP speaker.

section.t: Route Monitoring and Route Mirroring messages extend the per-peer session key with additional YANG nodes that identify the RIB and the individual route within it:

dl.dd: The AFI-SAFI of the route entry.
The RIB the route entry belongs to.
The NLRI prefix of the route entry, in the nlri container of its AFI-SAFI.
The BGP ADD-PATH path identifier (). Not included when ADD-PATH is not in use.

section.t: Initiation and Termination messages do not carry a Per-Peer Header; their Message Keys consist of only the node hostname and the message-type path. The per-peer session key is consistent across all lifecycle events for the same session (Peer Up, Statistics Report, Route Monitoring, and Peer Down), enabling deterministic topic compaction over the full session lifecycle. The session-start-timestamp of the bmp-session container is not part of the Message Key, so that the key remains the same when a BMP session is re-established.

The Message Key is encoded as a two-line byte string. The first line is the network node hostname; the second line is the YANG instance-identifier path. The separator between them is a single line feed character (LF, U+000A). The YANG path starts at the 'ietf-bmp-message' message node, whether the BMP message is the Message Value itself or is carried in the "payload" of a Network Telemetry Message (). The Message Key is therefore the same in both cases. A path through "payload" is not used, as "payload" is anydata and its content is not part of the 'ietf-telemetry-message' schema.

Each example below illustrates the Message Key, the Message Broker headers carrying the Schema ID, content type, and Partition Key, and the corresponding Message Value. The Message Value examples show BMP messages on their own; shows a BMP message carried in a Network Telemetry Message. Message Keys exceeding the line length are folded as described in .

section.name: BMP Partition Keys and Routing
section.t: Since BMP requires Message ordering for a monitored BGP RIB, and Message Brokers ensure Message ordering on partitions, a Partition Key and a custom partitioner logic is being introduced so that all BMP messages for a particular BGP RIB are hashed to on one partition. The Partition Key consists of the hostname of the network node.
In the partitioner implementation of the YANG Message Broker Producer, instead of the Message Key, the Partition Key MUST be used to deterministically hash BMP Messages to partitions.

section.name: Message Broker BMP Topic Naming
section.t: There are two Message Broker topics.

ul.li: bmp-state-changes-and-statistics: Containing all BMP messages in real-time
bmp-current-state: Containing all BMP message types, except statistics, topic compacted.

section.t: Optionally, an organization prefix can be prepended with a "-" separator. A Message Broker Consumer MAY consume either "bmp-state-changes-and-statistics", "bmp-current-state" or a subset depending on use case.

If a subset is consumed, the consumer hashes the Message Key, applies modulo with the number of partitions, and determines the partition from which it should consume messages bearing that Message Key.
To parse the Message Key, the consumer splits the byte string on newline (LF) characters. The first line is the node-name and the second the YANG path.
shows an example where "bmp-state-changes-and-statistics" is being used.

section.name: Message Broker Implementations
section.t: Topic, Partitioning and Message Keys are generic concepts of Message Brokers. There are two known Message Broker implementations supporting all features described in this document.

section.name: Apache Kafka
section.t: Apache Kafka supports Message Keys, Partitioning and Log Compaction. Per default, the partitioner logic uses Message Keys for deterministic partition Message distribution.
This document introduces "partition-key" in the Apache Kafka header to be used by the partitioner instead of the "key" (Message Key) when distributing Messages to the partitions.

section.name: Apache Pulsar
section.t: Apache Pulsar supports Message Keys, Partitioning and Topic Compaction. Per default, the partitioner logic uses Message Keys for deterministic partition Message distribution. Optionally, a dedicated ordering key can be used.
This document introduces "partition-key" which is to be used as ordering key.

section.name: BMP YANG Modules
section.t: The 'ietf-bmp-message' YANG module defines the top-level BMP message structure. It does not depend on 'ietf-telemetry-message': a BMP message can be used on its own or carried in the "payload" of a Network Telemetry Message (). It carries a mandatory version leaf from the BMP Common Header and a message-type choice covering all seven BMP message types: route-monitoring, statistics-report, peer-down-notification, peer-up-notification, initiation-message, termination-message, and route-mirroring-message.

The 'ietf-bmp-peer-header' module provides the peer-type typedef and the peer-header-flags grouping decoded from the BMP Per-Peer Header. It is imported by both 'ietf-bmp-message', for the per-peer header itself, and 'ietf-bmp-tlv', for the Extended Flags TLV, which extends the same flag bits to a variable-length byte sequence.

The 'ietf-bmp-statistics' module provides the statistics grouping used by statistics-report messages. Each Stat Type of the IANA 'BMP Statistics Types' registry ( ,, and ) is modeled as a named data node, for example routes-in-loc-rib, whose YANG type reflects the encoding of its Stat Data. Because a new Stat Type requires a new node, and thereby a module revision, a catch-all unknown list carries Stat Types that are not yet modeled, or whose Stat Data cannot be decoded, as raw binary, so no statistic has to be dropped.

The 'ietf-bgp-rib-entry' module provides the rib-entry grouping used by route-monitoring and route-mirroring messages. The route is represented once, in a flat structure, instead of being duplicated per AFI-SAFI and per RIB type. The 'afi-safi-type' and 'rib-type' leaves are siblings of the rib-entry container, so that consumers can select messages by AFI-SAFI and RIB without parsing the entry. 'rib-type' names the RIB the entry belongs to, using the RIB names of : loc-rib, adj-rib-in-pre, adj-rib-in-post, adj-rib-out-pre, or adj-rib-out-post. The optional 'path-id' (the received path-id for Adj-RIB-In, the sent path-id for Adj-RIB-Out) is a field of the rib-entry, as are the BGP path attributes and community attributes. The 'nlri' container carries the NLRI in a container named after the AFI-SAFI identity given by afi-safi-type, for example nlri/ipv4-unicast/prefix; other AFI-SAFIs can be added by augmenting the choice with a container in the same way. Instead of a route, a rib-entry can carry an end-of-rib marker, which represents the End-of-RIB marker () for the AFI-SAFI given by afi-safi-type and the RIB given by rib-type.

The 'ietf-bgp-open' module provides the bgp-open grouping, which carries the BGP OPEN message fields: protocol version, Autonomous System number, hold time, BGP identifier, and the negotiated capability list. It is used in peer-up-notification for both the sent and received OPEN messages.

The 'ietf-bmp-tlv' module provides groupings for the decoded content of BMP TLVs. The common grouping (sequence number, timestamps, extended flags, and an unknown-tlvs catch-all for TLV types not yet modeled) is used by all seven BMP message types. The other groupings are each specific to one message type: Initiation, Peer Up (including the Admin Label TLV of ), Termination, Peer Down, and Route Monitoring.

The 'ietf-bmp-telemetry-message' YANG module extends 'ietf-telemetry-message' for BMP. It defines the bmp identity, derived from session-protocol, and augments telemetry-message-metadata with the bmp-session container, which carries the BMP session metadata maintained by the data collector. Its use is described in .

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: This section is modeled after the template described in .

The "ietf-bmp-message", "ietf-bmp-telemetry-message", "ietf-bgp-rib-entry", "ietf-bgp-open", "ietf-bmp-tlv", "ietf-bmp-peer-header", and "ietf-bmp-statistics" YANG modules define one combined data model that is designed to be accessed via YANG-based management protocols, such as NETCONF and RESTCONF . These protocols have to use a secure transport layer (e.g., SSH , TLS , and QUIC ) and have to use mutual authentication.

The Network Configuration Access Control Model (NACM) provides the means to restrict access for particular NETCONF or RESTCONF users to a preconfigured subset of all available NETCONF or RESTCONF protocol operations and content.

There are a number of data nodes defined in this YANG module that are writable/creatable/deletable (i.e., "config true", which is the default). All writable data nodes are likely to be reasonably sensitive or vulnerable in some network environments. Write operations (e.g., edit-config) and delete operations to these data nodes without proper protection or authentication can have a negative effect on network operations. The following subtrees and data nodes have particular sensitivities/vulnerabilities:
"There are no particularly sensitive writable data nodes."

Some of the readable data nodes in this YANG module may be considered sensitive or vulnerable in some network environments. It is thus important to control read access (e.g., via get, get-config, or notification) to these data nodes. Specifically, the following subtrees and data nodes have particular sensitivities/ vulnerabilities:
"There are no particularly sensitive readable data nodes."
